newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PSE loses ground as blue chips retreat.
newsitem.headline: Czech PSE loses ground as blue chips retreat.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's two-session advancing streak came to a halt on Tuesday, as blue chips ran out of steam and the bourse itself lost hours of trading time due to technical problems.
Komercni Banka and CEZ both suffered modest losses to help push the PX50 index 2.2 points, or 0.39 percent, lower to 561.7.
In the previous two sessions, the index had jumped 2.7 percent as investors took advantage of a recent slump in the market to take new positions.
"There was a good opportunity to take profits last week, and many did," said one trader.

But he warned: "They are coming back somewhat now to take new positions, but I am afraid many will now leave the market for places such as Warsaw or Budapest, where the market is performing much better, and I can't blame them."
The PSE was forced to halt activity halfway through its continuous trading session because of technical problems, though it is expected the session will resume as planned on Wednesday.
The stoppage in trading put a dent in overall volume, with a modest 505,388 shares changing hands on turnover of 541.9 million crowns.
